questions.title: Count Frequency of Each Element in an Array
questions.problem_statement: Write a program to count the frequency of each element in an array. Optimize the time complexity to O(N) using a Hash Map or Frequency Array.
questions.hint: Iterate through the array and store element counts in a Map<Integer, Integer> or integer lookup array.

questions.title: Reverse Words in a Given String
questions.problem_statement: Given a sentence string, reverse the order of words without reversing the characters inside individual words, handling extra spaces cleanly.
questions.hint: Split the string by spaces, filter out empty tokens, and traverse backward or use a Stack.

questions.title: Java Exception Handling & Checked vs Unchecked Exceptions
questions.problem_statement: Differentiate between Checked and Unchecked exceptions in Java. Explain how the try-catch-finally block works and the effect of calling System.exit(0) inside a try block.
questions.hint: Checked exceptions are verified at compile-time (IOException, SQLException); Unchecked occur at runtime (NullPointerException, ArithmeticException).

questions.title: Method Overloading vs Overriding & Runtime Polymorphism
questions.problem_statement: Explain Runtime Polymorphism in Java using dynamic method dispatch. What happens when a parent reference variable points to a child class object?
questions.hint: The overridden method executed is determined dynamically at runtime based on the actual object created.

questions.title: SQL Subqueries & Second Highest Salary
questions.problem_statement: Write a SQL query to find the second highest salary from an Employee table without using the LIMIT or TOP clauses.
questions.hint: Use a subquery: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee).

questions.title: DBMS Normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF)
questions.problem_statement: Explain the concept of database Normalization. Detail the rules for First Normal Form (1NF), Second Normal Form (2NF), and Third Normal Form (3NF) to eliminate data redundancy.
questions.hint: 1NF requires atomic values; 2NF eliminates partial dependency; 3NF eliminates transitive dependency.

questions.title: Operating Systems CPU Scheduling Algorithms
questions.problem_statement: Compare First-Come First-Served (FCFS), Shortest Job First (SJF), and Round Robin (RR) CPU scheduling algorithms. Define turnaround time, waiting time, and starvation.
questions.hint: SJF provides optimal average waiting time; Round Robin uses time-slicing to prevent process starvation.

questions.title: Computer Networks IP Addressing & Subnetting Basics
questions.problem_statement: Explain IPv4 vs IPv6 addressing. What is a Subnet Mask, and how is it used to distinguish between network ID and host ID?
questions.hint: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses; IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses. Subnet mask bitwise ANDed with IP yields the network portion.

questions.title: Aptitude: Time and Work Efficiency
questions.problem_statement: A can complete a piece of work in 15 days and B can complete it in 20 days. If they work together for 4 days, what fraction of the total work is left unfinished?
questions.hint: 1 day combined work = 1/15 + 1/20 = 7/60. Work in 4 days = 28/60 = 7/15. Remaining = 1 - 7/15 = 8/15.

questions.title: Aptitude: Profit & Loss Discount Markup
questions.problem_statement: A trader marks his goods 25% above the cost price and allows a discount of 10% on the marked price. What is his net profit percentage?

questions.title: Aptitude: Mixture & Alligation Ratio
questions.problem_statement: In what ratio must milk at $40 per liter be mixed with water (at $0 per liter) so that selling the mixture at $35 per liter yields a profit of 16.66% (1/6)?
questions.hint: Cost price of mixture = 35 / (7/6) = $30. Use alligation: (30 - 0) : (40 - 30) = 30:10 = 3:1.

questions.title: Aptitude: Permutations & Combinations Word Formation
questions.problem_statement: In how many different ways can the letters of the word 'SYSTEM' be arranged?
questions.hint: Word length = 6 letters with 'S' repeated 2 times. Total arrangements = 6! / 2! = 720 / 2 = 360.

questions.title: Logical Reasoning: Blood Relations Problem
questions.problem_statement: Pointing to a photograph, a man said, 'I have no brother or sister, but that man's father is my father's son.' Whose photograph was it?
questions.hint: 'My father's son' means the man himself (since he has no siblings). So 'that man's father is myself'.

questions.title: Tell Me About Yourself
questions.problem_statement: Tell me about yourself, your educational background, core technical skills, and key accomplishments.
questions.hint: Deliver a structured summary of your academic background, technical proficiency, project highlights, and career goal.

questions.title: Why Do You Want to Join TCS?
questions.problem_statement: Why do you want to join Tata Consultancy Services (TCS)?
questions.hint: Highlight TCS's global reputation, Tata work ethics/values, career stability, continuous training (TCS iON/Elevate), and project exposure.

questions.title: Why Should We Hire You?
questions.problem_statement: Why should TCS hire you for this role?
questions.hint: Connect your solid CS fundamentals, problem-solving mindset, fast learning ability, and dedication with TCS's expectations.

questions.title: Explain Your Final-Year Project
questions.problem_statement: Explain your final-year academic or capstone project. What was your specific contribution?
questions.hint: Briefly state problem statement, technologies used, your personal module contribution, challenges overcome, and key outcome.

questions.title: Strengths and Weaknesses
questions.problem_statement: What are your greatest technical strengths and an area of weakness you are actively improving?
questions.hint: Mention a strong technical/soft skill and a real weakness along with actionable steps you are taking to grow.

questions.title: Relocation and Shift Flexibility
questions.problem_statement: Are you willing to relocate to any TCS location across India/globally and work in flexible project shifts?
questions.hint: Confirm flexibility, enthusiasm for learning in new environments, and professional commitment.

questions.title: Five-Year Career Vision
questions.problem_statement: Where do you see yourself in five years within TCS?
questions.hint: Express desire to master technical domain expertise, take on module leadership responsibilities, and contribute to enterprise projects.
